Variants.Content: Silverhall is the westward seat of House Brax, associated with traditions of silver mines, hills and noble horses. Minerals bring money, weapons, and the possibility of respectability to the family, but also bring the burden of labor management, mine accidents, transportation, and taxes. The nobles of the West are accustomed to weaving wealth into flags, armor, marriage contracts, and banquets, but a place like the Silver Hall knows it better: metal must be dug out of the darkness before wealth can become visible light. Its location connects it to the power network of Casterly Rock and also maintains the mine's own technical and human aspects.

Entry Silverhill Local families also relied on mining tunnels, pastures, mountain roads, gold and silver circulation and the market sheltered by Casterly Rock; if any road, well or dock failed, the price would fall first on them.

Entry Silverhill They also recognize the accents, laws, and credentials of the West; reputations can travel great distances from taverns, but true distances must still be measured by wheel, oar, or horse's hooves.

Entry Silverhill If you can supply supplies, avoid danger, and find a guide, it is worth marking in your itinerary; if you don't have these three things, no matter how loud your family name is, it won't be able to save the lost.
Entry Silverhill A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Silverhill They care about the mines, pastures, mountain roads, the circulation of gold and silver, and the market under the protection of Casterly Rock. They also look at whether seeds are left after the grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see the coat of arms, what they see is whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
